target.title: fix(browser): use boundary-aware home path replacement in chrome-mcp diagnostics
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`redactChromeMcpDiagnosticTextWithLocalPaths` in `extensions/browser/src/browser/chrome-mcp.ts` uses `text.split(homePath).join("~")` to redact home paths from diagnostic text — the same naive split/join pattern that was fixed in #98876 (`packages/terminal-core/src/display-string.ts`). This corrupts sibling paths that share the home prefix.

## Why This Change Was Made

The `split().join()` pattern matches the home directory as a substring anywhere in the text. When a sibling path like `/home/user2/project` appears in diagnostic output alongside the real home path `/home/user`, both get corrupted to `~2/project` instead of preserving the sibling.

## User Impact

Users with home directories that are a prefix of another path (e.g., `/home/user` vs `/home/user2`) see corrupted diagnostic output in browser MCP log messages.

## Evidence

**Real behavior proof — reproduced via node:**
```
Input:  "Error in /home/user2/project: file not found at /home/user/config.json"
OLD:    "Error in ~2/project: file not found at ~/config.json"  <- sibling corrupted
NEW:    "Error in /home/user2/project: file not found at ~/config.json"  <- fixed
```

**Validation:**
- tsgo typecheck: passed
- `pnpm test extensions/browser/src/browser/chrome-mcp.test.ts`: 46 tests passed
